title: Task-Centric Multimodal Learning for Cognitive Impairment Detection
description:
arXiv:2610.20906v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Dementia affects millions of older adults worldwide, yet early detection remains difficult outside clinical settings. Traditional models primarily rely on text or voice-based responses, capturing only a limited view of human cognition despite the inherently multimodal nature of human expression. This work proposes a contactless, multimodal screening framework that leverages video, audio, and text signals collected during structured voice-based interactions with Amazon Alexa. By incorporating these modalities, our approach captures a more holistic representation of human behavior encompassing speech patterns, vocal characteristics, facial expressions, and linguistic structure, which may enable more accurate detection of cognitive decline. Different participants completed three conversational tasks designed to probe spontaneous speech, comprehension, and recall. We pursued three objectives: (1) evaluate which of the three Alexa tasks provides the most informative cognitive signals, (2) compare the effectiveness of unimodal models, and (3) assess the benefits of multimodal fusion models. Task-level analysis shows that the video model achieves its best performance on Command-Reading, with an accuracy of 0.65 (AUC 0.69), while the audio model performs best on Question-Answering, reaching an accuracy of 0.67 (AUC 0.73). In contrast, the multimodal model demonstrates consistently stable performance across tasks, achieving an accuracy of 0.76 (AUC 0.75) on Command-Reading and 0.76 (AUC 0.73) on Question-Answering. These findings demonstrate that multimodal behavioral cues captured through naturalistic interactions can reliably distinguish MCI from healthy aging, highlighting the limitations of traditional diagnostic paradigms and supporting the shift toward multimodal, real-world cognitive assessment frameworks.

title: Understanding Blazor Component State
description:
Blazor components can respond to user interactions by updating component
state and rendering the UI again. A variable such as a Boolean can
control whether a section is visible, while event handlers connect
buttons and form submissions to C# methods. Data binding keeps input
values synchronized with component properties, and EditForm can use
validation attributes to check values before calling a submit handler.

@page "/component-state-demo"

<PageTitle>Component State Demo</PageTitle>

<div class="container py-5">
    <div class="card shadow-sm mx-auto" style="max-width: 500px;">
        <div class="card-body text-center">
            <h3 class="fw-bold mb-3">
                Understanding Component State
            </h3>

            <p class="text-secondary">
                The current counter value is stored in component state.
            </p>

            <div class="display-3 fw-bold text-primary mb-4">
                @count
            </div>

            <button class="btn btn-primary me-2"
                    @onclick="IncrementCount">
                <i class="bi bi-plus-circle me-1"></i>
                Increase
            </button>

            <button class="btn btn-outline-danger"
                    @onclick="ResetCount">
                <i class="bi bi-arrow-counterclockwise me-1"></i>
                Reset
            </button>

            <hr />

            <p class="mb-0">
                @message
            </p>
        </div>
    </div>
</div>

@code {
    private int count = 0;

    private string message = "Click Increase to update the state.";

    private void IncrementCount()
    {
        count++;

        message = $"The state changed. Current value: {count}";
    }

    private void ResetCount()
    {
        count = 0;

        message = "The counter state has been reset.";
    }
}


The following examples demonstrate these ideas through complete Razor
components. The code is kept in separate blocks so each component can be
copied and reviewed independently.

Shared state between components
What if two unrelated components need the same data?

For example:
A navigation bar displays the logged-in user's name.
A profile component displays the same user's information.
Both need to reflect changes to that information.
You can create a shared state service.

@page "/admin/membership-plans"
@attribute [Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authorization.Authorize(Roles = "Admin")]

@using System.Net.Http.Json
@using System.ComponentModel.DataAnnotations
@using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.Forms

@inject HttpClient Http
@inject IJSRuntime JS

<PageTitle>Manage Membership Plans</PageTitle>

<div class="container-fluid py-4">
    <div class="d-flex justify-content-between align-items-center flex-wrap gap-3 mb-4">
        <div>
            <h2 class="fw-bold mb-1">Manage Membership Plans</h2>
            <p class="text-secondary mb-0">Create and maintain gym membership plans.</p>
        </div>
        <button class="btn btn-primary" @onclick="OpenAddForm">
            <i class="bi bi-plus-circle me-1"></i>Add Plan
        </button>
    </div>

    <div class="card shadow-sm border-0 mb-4">
        <div class="card-body">
            <div class="row g-3">
                <div class="col-12 col-lg-4">
                    <label class="form-label">Search</label>
                    <input class="form-control"
                           @bind="searchText"
                           @bind:event="oninput"
                           placeholder="Search plan or gym..." />
                </div>

                <div class="col-12 col-md-6 col-lg-3">
                    <label class="form-label">Gym</label>
                    <select class="form-select" @bind="selectedGymId">
                        <option value="">All gyms</option>
                        @foreach (var gym in gyms)
                        {
                            <option value="@gym.Id">@gym.GymName</option>
                        }
                    </select>
                </div>

                <div class="col-12 col-md-6 col-lg-3">
                    <label class="form-label">Sort by</label>
                    <select class="form-select" @bind="sortBy">
                        <option value="name">Plan name</option>
                        <option value="price">Price</option>
                        <option value="duration">Duration</option>
                        <option value="gym">Gym</option>
                        <option value="status">Status</option>
                    </select>
                </div>

                <div class="col-12 col-lg-2">
                    <label class="form-label">Page size</label>
                    <select class="form-select" @bind="pageSize" @bind:after="ResetPage">
                        <option value="5">5</option>
                        <option value="10">10</option>
                        <option value="20">20</option>
                    </select>
                </div>
            </div>
        </div>
    </div>

    @if (isLoading)
    {
        <div class="text-center py-5">
            <div class="spinner-border text-primary"></div>
            <p class="text-secondary mt-2">Loading membership plans...</p>
        </div>
    }
    else if (!string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(errorMessage))
    {
        <div class="alert alert-danger">
            @errorMessage
            <button class="btn btn-sm btn-outline-danger ms-2"
                    @onclick="LoadDataAsync">Retry</button>
        </div>
    }
    else
    {
        <div class="card border-0 shadow-sm">
            <div class="table-responsive">
                <table class="table table-hover align-middle mb-0">
                    <thead class="table-light">
                        <tr>
                            <th>Plan</th>
                            <th>Gym</th>
                            <th>Price</th>
                            <th>Duration</th>
                            <th>Classes/week</th>
                            <th>Personal training</th>
                            <th>Locker</th>
                            <th>Guest access</th>
                            <th>Status</th>
                            <th class="text-end">Actions</th>
                        </tr>
                    </thead>
                    <tbody>
                        @foreach (var plan in PagedPlans)
                        {
                            <tr @key="plan.Id">
                                <td class="fw-semibold">@plan.PlanName</td>
                                <td>@plan.GymName</td>
                                <td>@plan.Price.ToString("C")</td>
                                <td>@plan.DurationInMonths months</td>
                                <td>@plan.ClassSessionsPerWeek</td>
                                <td>@plan.PersonalTrainingSessions</td>
                                <td>@(plan.LockerAccess ? "Yes" : "No")</td>
                                <td>
                                    @(plan.GuestAccess
                                        ? $"Yes ({plan.GuestPasses} passes)"
                                        : "No")
                                </td>
                                <td>
                                    <span class="badge @(plan.Status == "Active"
                                        ? "bg-success" : "bg-secondary")">
                                        @plan.Status
                                    </span>
                                </td>
                                <td class="text-end text-nowrap">
                                    <button class="btn btn-sm btn-outline-primary me-1"
                                            @onclick="() => OpenEditForm(plan.Id)">
                                        <i class="bi bi-pencil"></i>
                                    </button>
                                    <button class="btn btn-sm btn-outline-danger"
                                            @onclick="() => DeletePlanAsync(plan.Id)">
                                        <i class="bi bi-trash"></i>
                                    </button>
                                </td>
                            </tr>
                        }
                        @if (PagedPlans.Count == 0)
                        {
                            <tr>
                                <td colspan="10" class="text-center py-4 text-secondary">
                                    No membership plans found.
                                </td>
                            </tr>
                        }
                    </tbody>
                </table>
            </div>

            <div class="card-body d-flex flex-wrap justify-content-between align-items-center gap-3">
                <span class="text-secondary">
                    Showing @ShowingFrom–@ShowingTo of @FilteredPlans.Count plans
                </span>
                <div class="d-flex gap-2 align-items-center">
                    <button class="btn btn-outline-secondary btn-sm"
                            disabled="@(currentPage <= 1)"
                            @onclick="PreviousPage">Previous</button>
                    <span>Page @currentPage of @TotalPages</span>
                    <button class="btn btn-outline-secondary btn-sm"
                            disabled="@(currentPage >= TotalPages)"
                            @onclick="NextPage">Next</button>
                </div>
            </div>
        </div>
    }
</div>

@if (showForm)
{
    <div class="modal-backdrop-custom">
        <div class="card modal-card shadow-lg">
            <div class="card-header bg-white d-flex justify-content-between align-items-center">
                <h5 class="mb-0">@(isEditMode ? "Edit Plan" : "Add Plan")</h5>
                <button class="btn-close" @onclick="CloseForm"></button>
            </div>

            <div class="card-body">
                <EditForm Model="@formModel" OnValidSubmit="SavePlanAsync">
                    <DataAnnotationsValidator />
                    <ValidationSummary />

                    <div class="row g-3">
                        <div class="col-12">
                            <label class="form-label">Gym</label>
                            <InputSelect class="form-select" @bind-Value="formModel.GymId">
                                <option value="@Guid.Empty">Select gym</option>
                                @foreach (var gym in gyms.Where(g => g.Status == "Active"))
                                {
                                    <option value="@gym.Id">@gym.GymName</option>
                                }
                            </InputSelect>
                            <ValidationMessage For="@(() => formModel.GymId)" />
                        </div>

                        <div class="col-md-6">
                            <label class="form-label">Plan name</label>
                            <InputText class="form-control" @bind-Value="formModel.PlanName" />
                            <ValidationMessage For="@(() => formModel.PlanName)" />
                        </div>

                        <div class="col-md-6">
                            <label class="form-label">Price</label>
                            <InputNumber class="form-control" @bind-Value="formModel.Price" />
                            <ValidationMessage For="@(() => formModel.Price)" />
                        </div>

                        <div class="col-md-6">
                            <label class="form-label">Duration (months)</label>
                            <InputNumber class="form-control"
                                         @bind-Value="formModel.DurationInMonths" />
                            <ValidationMessage For="@(() => formModel.DurationInMonths)" />
                        </div>

                        <div class="col-md-6">
                            <label class="form-label">Class sessions per week</label>
                            <InputNumber class="form-control"
                                         @bind-Value="formModel.ClassSessionsPerWeek" />
                        </div>

                        <div class="col-md-6">
                            <label class="form-label">Personal training sessions</label>
                            <InputNumber class="form-control"
                                         @bind-Value="formModel.PersonalTrainingSessions" />
                        </div>

                        <div class="col-md-6">
                            <label class="form-label">Guest passes</label>
                            <InputNumber class="form-control" @bind-Value="formModel.GuestPasses" />
                        </div>

                        <div class="col-md-6">
                            <label class="form-label">Status</label>
                            <InputSelect class="form-select" @bind-Value="formModel.Status">
                                <option value="Active">Active</option>
                                <option value="Inactive">Inactive</option>
                            </InputSelect>
                        </div>

                        <div class="col-md-6 form-check ms-2">
                            <InputCheckbox class="form-check-input"
                                           @bind-Value="formModel.LockerAccess" />
                            <label class="form-check-label">Locker access</label>
                        </div>

                        <div class="col-md-6 form-check ms-2">
                            <InputCheckbox class="form-check-input"
                                           @bind-Value="formModel.GuestAccess" />
                            <label class="form-check-label">Guest access</label>
                        </div>
                    </div>

                    <div class="d-flex justify-content-end gap-2 mt-4">
                        <button type="button" class="btn btn-outline-secondary"
                                @onclick="CloseForm" disabled="@isSaving">
                            Cancel
                        </button>
                        <button type="submit" class="btn btn-primary" disabled="@isSaving">
                            @(isSaving ? "Saving..." : isEditMode ? "Update Plan" : "Save Plan")
                        </button>
                    </div>
                </EditForm>
            </div>
        </div>
    </div>
}

@code {
    public class GymOption
    {
        public Guid Id { get; set; }
        public string GymName { get; set; } = "";
        public string Status { get; set; } = "";
    }

    public class PlanRow
    {
        public Guid Id { get; set; }
        public Guid GymId { get; set; }
        public string GymName { get; set; } = "";
        public string PlanName { get; set; } = "";
        public decimal Price { get; set; }
        public int DurationInMonths { get; set; }
        public int ClassSessionsPerWeek { get; set; }
        public int PersonalTrainingSessions { get; set; }
        public bool LockerAccess { get; set; }
        public bool GuestAccess { get; set; }
        public int GuestPasses { get; set; }
        public string Status { get; set; } = "Active";
    }

    public class PlanForm
    {
        public Guid Id { get; set; }

        [Required]
        public Guid GymId { get; set; }

        [Required, StringLength(100)]
        public string PlanName { get; set; } = "";

        [Range(typeof(decimal), "0.01", "100000000")]
        public decimal Price { get; set; }

        [Range(1, 120)]
        public int DurationInMonths { get; set; } = 1;

        [Range(0, 100)]
        public int ClassSessionsPerWeek { get; set; }

        [Range(0, 100)]
        public int PersonalTrainingSessions { get; set; }

        public bool LockerAccess { get; set; }
        public bool GuestAccess { get; set; }

        [Range(0, 10000)]
        public int GuestPasses { get; set; }

        public string Status { get; set; } = "Active";
    }

    public class OperationResponse
    {
        public bool Success { get; set; }
        public string Message { get; set; } = "";
    }

    private List<GymOption> gyms = new();
    private List<PlanRow> plans = new();
    private PlanForm formModel = new();

    private bool isLoading;
    private bool isSaving;
    private bool showForm;
    private bool isEditMode;
    private string errorMessage = "";
    private string searchText = "";
    private string sortBy = "name";
    private string selectedGymId = "";
    private int currentPage = 1;
    private int pageSize = 10;

    private List<PlanRow> FilteredPlans
    {
        get
        {
            IEnumerable<PlanRow> query = plans;

            if (!string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(searchText))
            {
                query = query.Where(p =>
                    p.PlanName.Contains(searchText, StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase) ||
                    p.GymName.Contains(searchText, StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase));
            }

            if (Guid.TryParse(selectedGymId, out var gymId))
                query = query.Where(p => p.GymId == gymId);

            query = sortBy switch
            {
                "price" => query.OrderBy(p => p.Price),
                "duration" => query.OrderBy(p => p.DurationInMonths),
                "gym" => query.OrderBy(p => p.GymName),
                "status" => query.OrderBy(p => p.Status),
                _ => query.OrderBy(p => p.PlanName)
            };

            return query.ToList();
        }
    }

    private List<PlanRow> PagedPlans =>
        FilteredPlans.Skip((currentPage - 1) * pageSize).Take(pageSize).ToList();

    private int TotalPages => Math.Max(1, (int)Math.Ceiling(FilteredPlans.Count / (double)pageSize));
    private int ShowingFrom => FilteredPlans.Count == 0 ? 0 : ((currentPage - 1) * pageSize) + 1;
    private int ShowingTo => Math.Min(currentPage * pageSize, FilteredPlans.Count);

    protected override async Task OnInitializedAsync() => await LoadDataAsync();

    private async Task LoadDataAsync()
    {
        isLoading = true;
        errorMessage = "";

        try
        {
            gyms = await Http.GetFromJsonAsync<List<GymOption>>("api/GymCenter") ?? new();
            plans = await Http.GetFromJsonAsync<List<PlanRow>>("api/MembershipPlan") ?? new();
            currentPage = Math.Min(currentPage, TotalPages);
        }
        catch
        {
            errorMessage = "Unable to load gyms or membership plans. Verify the API endpoints.";
        }
        finally
        {
            isLoading = false;
        }
    }

    private void ResetPage() => currentPage = 1;
    private void PreviousPage() { if (currentPage > 1) currentPage--; }
    private void NextPage() { if (currentPage < TotalPages) currentPage++; }

    private void OpenAddForm()
    {
        formModel = new PlanForm();
        isEditMode = false;
        showForm = true;
    }

    private void OpenEditForm(Guid id)
    {
        var plan = plans.FirstOrDefault(p => p.Id == id);
        if (plan is null) return;

        formModel = new PlanForm
        {
            Id = plan.Id,
            GymId = plan.GymId,
            PlanName = plan.PlanName,
            Price = plan.Price,
            DurationInMonths = plan.DurationInMonths,
            ClassSessionsPerWeek = plan.ClassSessionsPerWeek,
            PersonalTrainingSessions = plan.PersonalTrainingSessions,
            LockerAccess = plan.LockerAccess,
            GuestAccess = plan.GuestAccess,
            GuestPasses = plan.GuestPasses,
            Status = plan.Status
        };

        isEditMode = true;
        showForm = true;
    }

    private async Task SavePlanAsync()
    {
        if (formModel.GymId == Guid.Empty)
        {
            await ShowMessageAsync("Select a gym", "Please select a gym for this plan.", false);
            return;
        }

        if (formModel.GuestAccess == false)
            formModel.GuestPasses = 0;

        isSaving = true;

        try
        {
            HttpResponseMessage response = isEditMode
                ? await Http.PutAsJsonAsync($"api/MembershipPlan/{formModel.Id}", formModel)
                : await Http.PostAsJsonAsync("api/MembershipPlan", formModel);

            var result = await response.Content.ReadFromJsonAsync<OperationResponse>();

            if (!response.IsSuccessStatusCode || result?.Success != true)
            {
                await ShowMessageAsync("Unable to save plan",
                    result?.Message ?? "The plan could not be saved.", false);
                return;
            }

            showForm = false;
            await LoadDataAsync();
            await ShowMessageAsync("Success", result.Message, true);
        }
        catch
        {
            await ShowMessageAsync("Error", "An error occurred while saving the plan.", false);
        }
        finally
        {
            isSaving = false;
        }
    }

    private async Task DeletePlanAsync(Guid id)
    {
        var confirmed = await JS.InvokeAsync<bool>(
            "gymUi.confirmDelete", "Delete membership plan?",
            "The API will check whether active subscriptions prevent deletion.");

        if (!confirmed) return;

        try
        {
            var response = await Http.DeleteAsync($"api/MembershipPlan/{id}");
            var result = await response.Content.ReadFromJsonAsync<OperationResponse>();

            if (!response.IsSuccessStatusCode || result?.Success != true)
            {
                await ShowMessageAsync("Unable to delete",
                    result?.Message ?? "The plan could not be deleted.", false);
                return;
            }

            await LoadDataAsync();
            await ShowMessageAsync("Success", result.Message, true);
        }
        catch
        {
            await ShowMessageAsync("Error", "An error occurred while deleting the plan.", false);
        }
    }

    private void CloseForm()
    {
        if (!isSaving) showForm = false;
    }

    private Task ShowMessageAsync(string title, string message, bool success) =>
        JS.InvokeVoidAsync("gymUi.showMessage", title, message, success).AsTask();
}

@page "/admin/memberships"
@attribute [Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authorization.Authorize(Roles = "Admin")]

@using System.Net.Http.Json
@using System.Globalization

@inject HttpClient Http

<PageTitle>Manage Memberships</PageTitle>

<div class="container-fluid py-4">
    <div class="mb-4">
        <h2 class="fw-bold mb-1">Manage Memberships</h2>
        <p class="text-secondary mb-0">
            Review subscriptions, registration dates, and membership status.
        </p>
    </div>

    <div class="card shadow-sm border-0 mb-4">
        <div class="card-body">
            <div class="row g-3">
                <div class="col-12 col-md-6 col-xl-4">
                    <label class="form-label">Search</label>
                    <input class="form-control"
                           @bind="searchText"
                           @bind:event="oninput"
                           placeholder="Member, gym, or plan..." />
                </div>

                <div class="col-12 col-md-6 col-xl-2">
                    <label class="form-label">Gym</label>
                    <select class="form-select" @bind="selectedGymId">
                        <option value="">All gyms</option>
                        @foreach (var gym in GymOptions)
                        {
                            <option value="@gym.Id">@gym.GymName</option>
                        }
                    </select>
                </div>

                <div class="col-12 col-md-6 col-xl-2">
                    <label class="form-label">Member</label>
                    <select class="form-select" @bind="selectedUserId">
                        <option value="">All members</option>
                        @foreach (var member in MemberOptions)
                        {
                            <option value="@member.Id">@member.MemberName</option>
                        }
                    </select>
                </div>

                <div class="col-12 col-md-6 col-xl-2">
                    <label class="form-label">Plan</label>
                    <select class="form-select" @bind="selectedPlanId">
                        <option value="">All plans</option>
                        @foreach (var plan in PlanOptions)
                        {
                            <option value="@plan.Id">@plan.PlanName</option>
                        }
                    </select>
                </div>

                <div class="col-12 col-md-6 col-xl-2">
                    <label class="form-label">Status</label>
                    <select class="form-select" @bind="selectedStatus">
                        <option value="">All statuses</option>
                        <option value="Pending">Pending</option>
                        <option value="Active">Active</option>
                        <option value="Expiring Soon">Expiring Soon</option>
                        <option value="Expired">Expired</option>
                        <option value="Cancelled">Cancelled</option>
                    </select>
                </div>

                <div class="col-12 col-md-6 col-xl-3">
                    <label class="form-label">Registered from</label>
                    <input type="date" class="form-control" @bind="registrationFrom" />
                </div>

                <div class="col-12 col-md-6 col-xl-3">
                    <label class="form-label">Registered to</label>
                    <input type="date" class="form-control" @bind="registrationTo" />
                </div>

                <div class="col-12 col-md-6 col-xl-3">
                    <label class="form-label">Sort by</label>
                    <select class="form-select" @bind="sortBy">
                        <option value="registration">Registration date</option>
                        <option value="member">Member</option>
                        <option value="gym">Gym</option>
                        <option value="plan">Plan</option>
                        <option value="start">Start date</option>
                        <option value="end">End date</option>
                        <option value="status">Status</option>
                    </select>
                </div>

                <div class="col-12 col-md-6 col-xl-3">
                    <label class="form-label">Page size</label>
                    <select class="form-select" @bind="pageSize" @bind:after="ResetPage">
                        <option value="5">5</option>
                        <option value="10">10</option>
                        <option value="20">20</option>
                    </select>
                </div>

                <div class="col-12 d-flex gap-2">
                    <button class="btn btn-outline-secondary" @onclick="ClearFilters">
                        Clear filters
                    </button>
                    <button class="btn btn-outline-primary" @onclick="LoadMembershipsAsync">
                        <i class="bi bi-arrow-clockwise me-1"></i>Refresh
                    </button>
                </div>
            </div>
        </div>
    </div>

    @if (isLoading)
    {
        <div class="text-center py-5">
            <div class="spinner-border text-primary"></div>
            <p class="text-secondary mt-2">Loading memberships...</p>
        </div>
    }
    else if (!string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(errorMessage))
    {
        <div class="alert alert-danger">
            @errorMessage
            <button class="btn btn-sm btn-outline-danger ms-2"
                    @onclick="LoadMembershipsAsync">Retry</button>
        </div>
    }
    else
    {
        <div class="card shadow-sm border-0">
            <div class="table-responsive">
                <table class="table table-hover align-middle mb-0">
                    <thead class="table-light">
                        <tr>
                            <th>Member</th>
                            <th>Gym</th>
                            <th>Plan</th>
                            <th>Registered</th>
                            <th>Start date</th>
                            <th>End date</th>
                            <th>Status</th>
                        </tr>
                    </thead>
                    <tbody>
                        @foreach (var membership in PagedMemberships)
                        {
                            var status = GetMembershipStatus(membership);

                            <tr @key="membership.Id">
                                <td>
                                    <div class="fw-semibold">@membership.MemberName</div>
                                    <div class="small text-secondary">@membership.MemberEmail</div>
                                </td>
                                <td>@membership.GymName</td>
                                <td>@membership.PlanName</td>
                                <td>@membership.RegistrationDate.ToString("dd MMM yyyy")</td>
                                <td>@membership.StartDate.ToString("dd MMM yyyy")</td>
                                <td>@membership.EndDate.ToString("dd MMM yyyy")</td>
                                <td>
                                    <span class="badge @GetStatusBadgeClass(status)">
                                        @status
                                    </span>
                                </td>
                            </tr>
                        }

                        @if (PagedMemberships.Count == 0)
                        {
                            <tr>
                                <td colspan="7" class="text-center py-4 text-secondary">
                                    No memberships match the selected filters.
                                </td>
                            </tr>
                        }
                    </tbody>
                </table>
            </div>

            <div class="card-body d-flex flex-wrap justify-content-between align-items-center gap-3">
                <span class="text-secondary">
                    Showing @ShowingFrom–@ShowingTo of @FilteredMemberships.Count memberships
                </span>

                <div class="d-flex gap-2 align-items-center">
                    <button class="btn btn-outline-secondary btn-sm"
                            disabled="@(currentPage <= 1)"
                            @onclick="PreviousPage">Previous</button>
                    <span>Page @currentPage of @TotalPages</span>
                    <button class="btn btn-outline-secondary btn-sm"
                            disabled="@(currentPage >= TotalPages)"
                            @onclick="NextPage">Next</button>
                </div>
            </div>
        </div>
    }
</div>

@code {
    public class MembershipRowModel
    {
        public Guid Id { get; set; }
        public Guid GymId { get; set; }
        public Guid MembershipPlanId { get; set; }
        public Guid UserId { get; set; }

        public string GymName { get; set; } = "";
        public string MemberName { get; set; } = "";
        public string MemberEmail { get; set; } = "";
        public string PlanName { get; set; } = "";

        public DateTime RegistrationDate { get; set; }
        public DateTime StartDate { get; set; }
        public DateTime EndDate { get; set; }

        // Expected values: Pending, Active, Cancelled, Expired.
        // Expiring Soon is derived from an active membership near its end date.
        public string Status { get; set; } = "";
    }

    public class GymOption
    {
        public Guid Id { get; set; }
        public string GymName { get; set; } = "";
    }

    public class MemberOption
    {
        public Guid Id { get; set; }
        public string MemberName { get; set; } = "";
    }

    public class PlanOption
    {
        public Guid Id { get; set; }
        public string PlanName { get; set; } = "";
    }

    private List<MembershipRowModel> memberships = new();
    private bool isLoading;
    private string errorMessage = "";
    private string searchText = "";
    private string selectedGymId = "";
    private string selectedUserId = "";
    private string selectedPlanId = "";
    private string selectedStatus = "";
    private string sortBy = "registration";
    private DateTime? registrationFrom;
    private DateTime? registrationTo;
    private int currentPage = 1;
    private int pageSize = 10;

    private List<GymOption> GymOptions =>
        memberships.GroupBy(m => m.GymId)
            .Select(g => new GymOption
            {
                Id = g.Key,
                GymName = g.First().GymName
            })
            .OrderBy(g => g.GymName)
            .ToList();

    private List<MemberOption> MemberOptions =>
        memberships.GroupBy(m => m.UserId)
            .Select(g => new MemberOption
            {
                Id = g.Key,
                MemberName = g.First().MemberName
            })
            .OrderBy(m => m.MemberName)
            .ToList();

    private List<PlanOption> PlanOptions =>
        memberships.GroupBy(m => m.MembershipPlanId)
            .Select(g => new PlanOption
            {
                Id = g.Key,
                PlanName = g.First().PlanName
            })
            .OrderBy(p => p.PlanName)
            .ToList();

    private List<MembershipRowModel> FilteredMemberships
    {
        get
        {
            IEnumerable<MembershipRowModel> query = memberships;

            if (!string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(searchText))
            {
                query = query.Where(m =>
                    m.MemberName.Contains(searchText, StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase) ||
                    m.MemberEmail.Contains(searchText, StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase) ||
                    m.GymName.Contains(searchText, StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase) ||
                    m.PlanName.Contains(searchText, StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase));
            }

            if (Guid.TryParse(selectedGymId, out var gymId))
                query = query.Where(m => m.GymId == gymId);

            if (Guid.TryParse(selectedUserId, out var userId))
                query = query.Where(m => m.UserId == userId);

            if (Guid.TryParse(selectedPlanId, out var planId))
                query = query.Where(m => m.MembershipPlanId == planId);

            if (registrationFrom.HasValue)
                query = query.Where(m => m.RegistrationDate.Date >= registrationFrom.Value.Date);

            if (registrationTo.HasValue)
                query = query.Where(m => m.RegistrationDate.Date <= registrationTo.Value.Date);

            if (!string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(selectedStatus))
                query = query.Where(m => GetMembershipStatus(m) == selectedStatus);

            query = sortBy switch
            {
                "member" => query.OrderBy(m => m.MemberName),
                "gym" => query.OrderBy(m => m.GymName),
                "plan" => query.OrderBy(m => m.PlanName),
                "start" => query.OrderBy(m => m.StartDate),
                "end" => query.OrderBy(m => m.EndDate),
                "status" => query.OrderBy(m => GetMembershipStatus(m)),
                _ => query.OrderByDescending(m => m.RegistrationDate)
            };

            return query.ToList();
        }
    }

    private List<MembershipRowModel> PagedMemberships =>
        FilteredMemberships.Skip((currentPage - 1) * pageSize).Take(pageSize).ToList();

    private int TotalPages =>
        Math.Max(1, (int)Math.Ceiling(FilteredMemberships.Count / (double)pageSize));

    private int ShowingFrom =>
        FilteredMemberships.Count == 0 ? 0 : ((currentPage - 1) * pageSize) + 1;

    private int ShowingTo =>
        Math.Min(currentPage * pageSize, FilteredMemberships.Count);

    protected override async Task OnInitializedAsync() => await LoadMembershipsAsync();

    private async Task LoadMembershipsAsync()
    {
        isLoading = true;
        errorMessage = "";

        try
        {
            memberships =
                await Http.GetFromJsonAsync<List<MembershipRowModel>>(
                    "api/Subscription/AdminList") ?? new();

            currentPage = Math.Min(currentPage, TotalPages);
        }
        catch
        {
            errorMessage =
                "Unable to load memberships. Check that api/Subscription/AdminList exists and returns the expected data.";
        }
        finally
        {
            isLoading = false;
        }
    }

    private static string GetMembershipStatus(MembershipRowModel membership)
    {
        // Cancellation always takes precedence over date-based statuses.
        if (string.Equals(membership.Status, "Cancelled",
                StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase))
            return "Cancelled";

        if (string.Equals(membership.Status, "Pending",
                StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase) ||
            membership.StartDate.Date > DateTime.Today)
            return "Pending";

        if (membership.EndDate.Date < DateTime.Today ||
            string.Equals(membership.Status, "Expired",
                StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase))
            return "Expired";

        var daysRemaining = (membership.EndDate.Date - DateTime.Today).Days;

        if (daysRemaining <= 7)
            return "Expiring Soon";

        return "Active";
    }

    private static string GetStatusBadgeClass(string status) => status switch
    {
        "Pending" => "bg-warning text-dark",
        "Active" => "bg-success",
        "Expiring Soon" => "bg-info text-dark",
        "Expired" => "bg-secondary",
        "Cancelled" => "bg-danger",
        _ => "bg-secondary"
    };

    private void ResetPage() => currentPage = 1;
    private void PreviousPage() { if (currentPage > 1) currentPage--; }
    private void NextPage() { if (currentPage < TotalPages) currentPage++; }

    private void ClearFilters()
    {
        searchText = "";
        selectedGymId = "";
        selectedUserId = "";
        selectedPlanId = "";
        selectedStatus = "";
        registrationFrom = null;
        registrationTo = null;
        sortBy = "registration";
        currentPage = 1;
    }
}

title: Making every stage of medical device document assessment with large language models deterministic
description:
arXiv:2610.21300v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: To show that a medical device complies with regulation, experts judge whether documents and records meet each requirement and record the judgment for others to verify. For each assessment item that experts define, large language models could prepare a preliminary assessment: a label such as Satisfied or Not satisfied, a reason and quoted evidence. We sent fourteen commercial deployments of such models (seven models from three providers, through six routes) the same request repeatedly, with the deterministic sampling settings each accepted; every deployment returned differing assessments for at least one request, and in twelve the label changed. Reducing reasoning where the interface allows it did not reduce the variation, and prompts of retrieved passages removed it only for the smallest models. The same open-weight model was reproducible or not depending only on how it was served. A pipeline we built to be deterministic at every stage -- text extraction and optical character recognition (OCR), chunking, embedding, indexing, retrieval and inference -- returned byte-identical output at each stage across reruns, interruptions, edits, machines of one graphics processing unit (GPU) model and days, for blood glucose meter and infusion pump documents. OCR, embedding and approximate retrieval varied when their own serving was not made invariant, and outputs changed with the GPU model and with the inference engine's scheduling settings, which therefore belong in the recorded configuration. End-to-end determinism is achievable and gives a testable basis for audit and change control.

title: Create record using JooqTemplate
description:
Using JooqTemplate requires no code generation and no XML configuration.

Add Dependency

gradle:

implementation 'net.sf.sprtool:sprtool-jooq:1.7.0'

maven:

<dependency>
    <groupId>net.sf.sprtool</groupId>
    <artifactId>sprtool-jooq</artifactId>
    <version>1.7.0</version>
</dependency>

Inject JooqTemplate 

import net.sf.sprtool.jooq.JooqTemplate;

@Autowired
private JooqTemplate jt;

Using JooqTemplate

Inserting a Product Record

Set field values by building a Map, then call the insert method to insert a product record:

Map<String, Object> product = new HashMap<>();
product.put("name", "Phone");
product.put("price", 3999.00);
product.put("stock", 100);
product.put("category", "digital");

int result = jt.insert("product", product);
// result == 1 means the insert succeeded

Inserting a User Record (Partial Fields)

When only some fields are set, the unset fields are written as null:

Map<String, Object> user = new HashMap<>();
user.put("name", "Jack ku");
user.put("nick_name", "As");

int result = jt.insert("user", user);
// The remaining fields (such as avatar_address, birthday) are null

Converting a Java Bean to a Map Automatically

Use JooqMaps.toSnakeCase to automatically convert a camelCase-named Bean into a snake_case-named Map, then perform the insert:

// UserEntity has properties such as name / nickName / avatarAddress / birthday
Map<String, Object> values = JooqMaps.toSnakeCase(userEntity);
int result = jt.insert("user", values);
// To keep fields whose values are null, use JooqMaps.toSnakeCaseWithNull(userEntity);

Inserting an Empty Map

When an empty Map is passed, a record is still inserted (each field uses its default value or null):

int result = jt.insert("order", new HashMap<>());
// result == 1; a record with all fields null was inserted

Exception Cases

  • Passing a null Map throws NullPointerException / IllegalArgumentException.
  • When the table name does not exist, an exception is thrown and the message contains the table name.

title: Letter to Last-Tuesday-Me: The Baseline Probe I Skipped on a Free Cloud Box
description:
Letter to Last-Tuesday-Me: The Baseline Probe I Skipped on a Free Cloud Box

I lost a day to a sandbox, not to a model.
The patch was fine on my laptop and wrong on the remote box.
Fixing the box took twenty minutes. Finding out it was the box took eight hours.

That is the whole letter. Here is the version with receipts.

The Story in Four Lines

An agent drafted a small refactor. I ran it locally: green. I copied it to a free cloud server and ran the same suite: red.

I assumed the model was wrong. I rewrote the prompt three times. I read the diff four times. The diff was never the problem.

The remote box had a lower open-file limit and a slower disk. My test wrote hundreds of temp files. Locally it survived. On the box it hit the limit partway through, and the suite reported the failure as a logic error.

Nothing in that story is exotic. Everything in it is preventable with one script and one habit.

Mistake 1: I Measured the Code Before the Box

I had a benchmark for the patch and no baseline for the host.
A benchmark without a baseline is a rumor.

Fix: capture a baseline before the first agent call. That is step 2 of my harness.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# probe.sh — record the box before any patch lands
set -euo pipefail
out="${1:-baseline.json}"
args=(
  --arg captured_at "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)"
  --arg kernel "$(uname -sr)"
  --arg python "$(python3 -V 2>&1)"
  --arg umask "$(umask)"
  --argjson cpu_count "$(nproc)"
  --argjson mem_mib "$(awk '/MemTotal/ {print int($2/1024)}' /proc/meminfo)"
  --argjson disk_free_mib "$(df -Pm / | awk 'NR==2 {print $4}')"
  --argjson tmp_free_mib "$(df -Pm /tmp | awk 'NR==2 {print $4}')"
  --argjson open_files "$(ulimit -n)"
  --argjson user_procs "$(ulimit -u)"
)
jq -n "${args[@]}" '{
  captured_at: $captured_at,
  kernel: $kernel,
  python: $python,
  umask: $umask,
  cpu_count: $cpu_count,
  mem_mib: $mem_mib,
  disk_free_mib: $disk_free_mib,
  tmp_free_mib: $tmp_free_mib,
  open_files: $open_files,
  user_procs: $user_procs
}' > "$out"
echo "wrote $out"

Run it twice: once right after provisioning, once before the failing run.
Then diff the two files instead of diffing your opinions.

diff <(jq -S . baseline.before.json) <(jq -S . baseline.after.json)

If open_files or tmp_free_mib moved, you have a resource story, not a logic story.

Next, add a reference workload so timings mean something. Two runs of a fixed, boring task.

run_ref() {
  local label="$1" start end
  start=$(date +%s%N)
  for i in $(seq 1 200); do sha256sum /etc/hostname > /dev/null; done
  end=$(date +%s%N)
  echo "$label $(( (end - start) / 1000000 )) ms"
}
run_ref ref-a
run_ref ref-b

Fill those milliseconds from your own box. I am deliberately not publishing mine, because a number from my machine would only mislead yours.

Mistake 2: I Let the Model Write Straight into the Shell

Step 4 of my harness stages model output as a file, never as a command.
The model is an untrusted text generator. Treat it that way.

# ask, but do not execute
agent_draft() {
  local prompt_file="$1" out_file="$2"
  mkdir -p "$(dirname "$out_file")"
  # placeholder client — substitute your own model CLI
  your-model-cli --prompt "$(cat "$prompt_file")" > "$out_file"
  sha256sum "$out_file" | tee "$out_file.sha256"
}

I keep a short path allowlist in front of git apply. If a patch touches anything outside src/ and test/, the run stops before the shell sees it.

The gate matters less than the habit. The habit is: no model bytes reach bash directly.

This is the part where MonkeyCode participates. I draft patches against its free model access, then run the suite on its free server option, so early iteration does not require a billing decision. Disclosure: This article was prepared as part of MonkeyCode's product outreach.

Both of those are availability claims, not performance claims. Check the current limits on the project page before you build a habit on them, because free tiers change.

Mistake 3: I Kept No Receipt, So I Blamed the Wrong Layer

I had no record of what ran. So every failure looked like a model failure.
A receipt turns an argument into a lookup.

run_receipt() {
  local run_id="$1" patch="$2" start_ms end_ms code
  start_ms=$(date +%s%N)
  if git apply --check "$patch" && git apply "$patch"; then
    code=0
  else
    code=1
  fi
  end_ms=$(date +%s%N)
  local args=(
    --arg run_id "$run_id"
    --arg commit "$(git rev-parse HEAD)"
    --arg patch_sha256 "$(sha256sum "$patch" | cut -d' ' -f1)"
    --arg baseline_sha256 "$(sha256sum baseline.json | cut -d' ' -f1)"
    --argjson exit_code "$code"
    --argjson wall_ms "$(( (end_ms - start_ms) / 1000000 ))"
  )
  jq -n "${args[@]}" '{
    run_id: $run_id,
    commit: $commit,
    patch_sha256: $patch_sha256,
    baseline_sha256: $baseline_sha256,
    exit_code: $exit_code,
    wall_ms: $wall_ms
  }' > "runs/$run_id.json"
}

Add model_id and tokens_used by hand from the provider console. Do not guess them, and do not infer them from wall time.

Now a failure has a shape. Match the shape, skip the guesswork.

Symptom Likely layer First check
Passes locally, dies at file ~100 Host limits ulimit -n, baseline diff
Same prompt, different patch twice Model nondeterminism patch_sha256 in two receipts
Job stops mid-run with no stack trace Quota or rate limit Provider console, not the code
Permission denied after a copy umask or mount flags umask in baseline.json
Tests slow only on the box Disk or CPU class run_ref timings
Patch applies, tests unchanged Stale commit commit field in the receipt

Seven rows, one hour of measurement. That table is the day I got back.

The Harness, Numbered

  1. Freeze the target: git rev-parse HEAD > runs/commit.txt.
  2. Capture the box: ./probe.sh baseline.json.
  3. Time a reference workload twice with run_ref.
  4. Draft the patch with the model; keep raw output in out/patch.raw.
  5. Gate the patch with the path allowlist; stop on any miss.
  6. Apply inside run_receipt; write the receipt before running tests.
  7. Run the suite. Attach the receipt to any failure report.

Seven steps, roughly ten minutes to assemble once.
After that, every failure names its own layer without a rewrite of the prompt.

Limitations and Who Should Skip This

  • Do not put secrets, customer data, or private keys on a shared free box.
  • Do not use this loop for GPU training, long-lived daemons, or licensed datasets.
  • Do not treat free-tier limits as stable; rerun probe.sh after every reprovision.
  • Do not run model output with sudo. Not once, not in a container, not with a note.
  • If your team already has pinned CI runners with reproducible images, you may not need a second box. You still need the receipts.

The Letter, Short Version

Dear last-Tuesday-me: the diff was fine.
You skipped the baseline, you piped the model, and you kept no receipt.
Next time, capture the box first and let the failure name itself.

If you want to try that loop without a billing decision, start with the free model access and the free server option, run probe.sh once, and write one receipt before you trust anything the agent produces.

    event.preventDefault(); if (!administrator || busy) return;

      const teamName = canonicalTeamName(team);
      const [userHash, administratorHash] = await Promise.all([hashPassword(teamPassword), hashPassword(adminPassword)]);
      if (!teamName || s.teams.some(t => t.toLowerCase() === teamName.toLowerCase())) throw new Error('This team already exists.');

Both access levels sign in through the same team login.</p>{error && <p className="form-error" role="alert">{error}</p>}<div className="modal-actions"><Button variant="primary" type="submit" icon="plus" disabled={busy}>{busy ? 'url' : 'text'} value={settings[key]} onChange={e => setSettings(v => ({ ...v, [key]: e.target.value }))} placeholder={placeholder}/></Field>)}<Field label="Bounded retry limit"><input type="number" min={0} max={5} value={settings.retryLimit} onChange={e => setSettings(v => ({ ...v, retryLimit: Number(e.target.value) }))}/></Field><div className="modal-actions"><Button type="submit" variant="primary">Save connection settings</Button></div></form></section>
    : <><section className="card padded"><h2>Team workspace</h2><p className="supporting-copy">Back up your workspace records and review activity.</p><div className="row-actions margin-top"><Button icon="external" onClick={() => download('ccil-studio-backup.json', JSON.stringify(s, null, 2), 'application/json')}>Export metadata backup</Button><Button icon="upload" onClick={() => file.current.click()}>Import metadata backup</Button><Button onClick={() => setDialog('reset')}>Reset application records</Button><input ref={file} className="sr-only" type="file" accept=".json" onChange={importBackup}/></div>{error && <p className="form-error" role="alert">{error}</p>}<Note>Metadata backups include source text and conversations. title: Exploring the Design Space of Permutation Diffusion LLMs
description:
arXiv:2610.20635v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Permutation generation with language models requires both text-conditioned ranking and a global one-to-one assignment between candidates and output positions. We study this problem through three diffusion-LLM parameterizations: hard-assignment prediction over shuffled candidate-index sequences, soft-assignment prediction over doubly stochastic matrices, and direct ordering-score prediction followed by sorting. The three families place permutation constraints at different stages of prediction and decoding and therefore support different training objectives and sampling procedures. We evaluate these designs on recommendation reranking across three Amazon domains with candidate sets of size 10 and 20. At one function evaluation, the hard- and soft-assignment variants achieve Recall@1 comparable to a constrained masked-diffusion baseline, whereas direct ordering-score prediction guarantees valid permutations without Hungarian assignment or Sinkhorn normalization. Additional function evaluations do not consistently improve ranking quality, and their effect depends strongly on the state representation and training objective. These results show that corruption, prediction parameterization, objective, and decoder should be designed jointly for permutation diffusion with language-model denoisers.

title: Semantic Alignment of EEG and Text: A Contrastive Learning Framework for Decoding Imagined Speech
description:
arXiv:2610.20766v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Imagined speech decoding from EEG offers a promising route toward naturalistic brain-computer interfaces. Traditional closed-set classifiers treat semantic categories as independent labels and do not explicitly exploit relationships among linguistic intents, limiting output flexibility. We adapt a multimodal contrastive learning framework to imagined speech, aligning EEG trials with language representations in the embedding space of a frozen pretrained text encoder. An EEG encoder is trained with a composite objective combining semantically reweighted EEG-sentence alignment and text-prototype-based class discrimination, encouraging semantic structure while preserving separability among 39 intent categories. We evaluate the approach on the Chisco imagined speech dataset across five subjects, reporting Top-k accuracy, macro-F1, and balanced pairwise matching accuracy (2v2). We also investigate maximum EEG-text cosine similarity (MaxCosine) as an intrinsic indicator of decoding reliability and probe semantic structure beyond category labels using five evaluation-time semantic axes and a qualitative Semantic Gallery Probe (SGP) with previously unseen candidate sentences. The contrastive framework achieved decoding performance comparable to a task-optimized closed-set classifier while mapping EEG into a frozen language embedding space. MaxCosine identified subsets of held-out trials with higher Top-1 and Top-5 accuracy across subjects. Evaluation-time semantic axes showed mean agreement above the 50% chance reference across all five dimensions, and the SGP qualitatively illustrated direct comparison with unseen candidate sentences. Together, these findings suggest that EEG-language alignment can retain comparable fixed-intent decoding while supporting similarity-based retrieval, intrinsic reliability ranking, and evaluation of broader semantic structure.

title: On-Policy Residual Learning for Diffusion Language Models
description:
arXiv:2610.20687v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Residual context is key to unlocking the speed-quality Pareto frontier of diffusion language models (DLMs) by carrying forward predictive distributions across denoising steps. Yet turning this seemingly simple mechanism into an effective learning paradigm is far from simple: there is no clear recipe for how residual context should be learned. We introduce ORL, a framework for on-policy residual learning in DLMs. Algorithmically, we identify that residual learning is inherently on-policy. ORL learns from model-induced residual trajectories on the fly and introduces an entropy-contraction objective that sharpens predictions as the model revisits its own predictions. System-wise, exact residual supervision requires capturing, retaining, and reprocessing many trajectory-dependent states. ORL co-designs the algorithm with asynchronous residual capture and transport, specialized block-diffusion attention, and packed compute-balanced training, making it practical at scale. On a 4B DLM converted from Qwen3-4B, ORL improves tokens per forward (TPF) by up to 6.2x and, with our dlmrt engine, end-to-end throughput by approximately 6.9x at comparable or better quality. In single-request serving on one H100, this mode achieves a stronger speed-quality Pareto frontier than autoregressive models with EAGLE3 and DFlash speculative decoding under both strict and relaxed verification, running 1.74x faster than DFlash at matched accuracy. ORL also transfers to existing DLMs: on LLaDA-2.1-mini, 36 H100-hours and 4.2M self-generated tokens, about 10x less data than prior LLaDA recipes, yield up to 1.5x higher TPF and up to 3x higher throughput at comparable quality, and on DiffusionGemma, ORL raises TPF by 1.1-1.2x. With dlmrt and NVFP4 quantization, ORL models decode a single request at up to 5,046 tokens/s on one B200, 7,708 on eight B200s, and 2,788 on a consumer RTX 5090, with comparable quality.

title: Our Hysteria2 connections died after every upload speed test. The fix was 37 lines.
description:
We build Colitu, a VPN with open-source apps for Android, iOS, Windows, Linux and a browser extension. The apps carry traffic over several transports. Hysteria2 is a QUIC-based one that our apps prefer on many networks, because it holds up well on lossy mobile links.

The apps also check their own connection. Every 5 seconds they send a small request through the tunnel. If three checks in a row get no answer within 4 seconds, the transport is declared dead, and traffic moves to a TCP spare that is already connected. Users stay online. But a transport that keeps getting declared dead is a bug, even if nobody notices.

How we noticed

We were testing port hopping for Hysteria2 on an Android phone on home Wi-Fi. With port hopping, the client moves to a new UDP port every ~30 seconds, so networks that slow down long-running UDP flows have a harder time doing it.

Hopping itself worked. We saw five hops, and the server's replies arrived on every new port.

Then we ran a speed test. Hysteria2 carried traffic for about 50–60 seconds and then stopped for good. The health check gave up and traffic went to the spare. It happened every time.

We repeated the test on a server without port hopping and got the same result. So hopping was not the cause; it was just the test that showed the bug.

What the packets said

We captured traffic on the phone. After the stall:

  • the QUIC connection was alive: ACKs and small control packets went both ways;
  • UDP datagrams still flowed: DNS and the apps' own QUIC traffic, which Hysteria carries as datagrams;
  • the client sent no new TCP stream data at all, not even for brand-new requests;
  • the server logged nothing unusual.

A connection that is alive but will not send stream data points at flow control, not at the network.

What we ruled out first

We tested each of these instead of assuming:

Suspect How we tested it Result
ISP shaping UDP read the capture packets kept flowing both ways; the client stopped sending
Probe starvation under load watched after the load ended the stall lasted for minutes after the load was gone
Congestion control A/B build with Reno instead of BBR died the same way
Xray's "Chrome parrot" QUIC mode A/B build with it disabled died the same way
Stream limit counted streams ~90 open against a limit of 1,024
Many connections in general 1,400 short sequential connections all fine

One more thing we tried: a bigger flow-control window (64 MB per connection, 4 MB per stream). It did not fix anything. It only delayed the stall: with 6 parallel streams it failed in round 3, with 20 streams immediately. That was the strongest hint about where to look.

Reproducing it on one PC

To get rid of the network entirely, we built the official Hysteria server v2.11.0 from source and ran it on loopback with an Xray 26.10.10 client. A small Python harness opened parallel uploads through the client, aborted them with a TCP reset, and then checked whether new requests still worked.

The only thing we changed between runs was how the upload's destination behaved:

Target mode What the destination does Connection stalled?
fast reads everything no
slow reads 1 MB/s no
upclose closes the connection first no
stall stops reading but keeps the connection open yes: 0 of 5 new requests worked, no recovery in 30 s

An upload speed test behaves exactly like stall. The test server stops reading once it has measured enough, while the browser's upload request is still open.

The mechanism

QUIC limits how much unread data a peer may have in flight, per stream and for the whole connection. Hysteria's defaults are 8 MB per stream and 20 MB per connection. Received bytes count against both windows until the application actually reads them.

Here is what happens:

client (Xray)                 Hysteria server                 target
     |  upload on stream A  ->  |  io.Copy(target, stream A) -> |
     |                          |                               |  stops reading,
     |                          |  target's TCP buffer full     |  keeps conn open
     |                          |  write to target BLOCKS       |
     |                          |  -> server stops reading A    |
     |  A's unread bytes keep counting against the connection window
     |  (a few streams like A fill all 20 MB)
     |
     |  new request on stream B: blocked, no connection credit left
     |  writer for A: blocked on the same window, so the client
     |  never gets to cancel A either
     |
     |  UDP datagrams: not flow-controlled -> still flowing
  1. The client uploads through a Hysteria2 stream. The server dials the target over TCP and copies the stream into it.
  2. The target stops reading but does not close. Its receive buffer fills, the server's Write into the target blocks, and the server stops reading from the stream.
  3. The stream's unread upload data keeps occupying the connection-level receive window. A few such streams use up the whole window. From then on the client cannot send on any stream of the connection, including brand-new ones.
  4. The client never gives the stream up, because its own writer is blocked on the same window. On an instrumented server, the "stream given up" signal only arrived when we killed the client process.
  5. UDP datagrams are not covered by stream flow control, which is why DNS kept working and the connection looked healthy.

Interesting detail: we first suspected the server never calls CancelRead on dead streams. That was wrong. The stream's Close already does that. The real problem is that nothing ever reaches that Close, because the copy into the target is stuck in a blocking Write.

The fix

The server cannot tell a stalled target from a slow one by looking at the stream. It can tell by progress: a single write that makes no progress for a long time.

So the patch does two things:

  1. Every write into a TCP target gets a fresh 10-second budget. If one write makes no progress for 10 s, the target is closed. The normal cleanup then closes the stream, which releases its share of the connection window.
  2. When the client gives the stream up, the target is closed immediately, so both copy directions end even when the target is silent.

A slow target that keeps moving is never cut off, because every write starts a new timer. Only a target that has stopped accepting data is closed.

This is the version we sent upstream in PR #1703:

if h.config.TCPStallTimeout > 0 {
    guard := newStallGuardConn(tConn, h.config.TCPStallTimeout)
    tConn = guard
    stop := context.AfterFunc(stream.Context(), func() { _ = guard.Close() })
    defer stop()
}

// stallGuardConn closes the wrapped connection when a single Write makes no
// progress for timeout, and makes Close idempotent. Every Write gets a fresh
// timeout, so a slow target that keeps accepting data is never closed.
type stallGuardConn struct {
    net.Conn
    timeout   time.Duration
    timer     *time.Timer
    closeOnce sync.Once
    closeErr  error
}

func newStallGuardConn(conn net.Conn, timeout time.Duration) *stallGuardConn {
    c := &stallGuardConn{Conn: conn, timeout: timeout}
    c.timer = time.AfterFunc(timeout, func() { _ = c.Close() })
    c.timer.Stop()
    return c
}

func (c *stallGuardConn) Write(p []byte) (int, error) {
    c.timer.Reset(c.timeout)
    n, err := c.Conn.Write(p)
    c.timer.Stop()
    return n, err
}

func (c *stallGuardConn) Close() error {
    c.closeOnce.Do(func() { c.closeErr = c.Conn.Close() })
    return c.closeErr
}

Our production build (v2.11.0-colitu1) does the same thing with SetWriteDeadline before each write. For the upstream version we made three changes:

  • the check closes the connection from a timer, so it only needs Close and works with any net.Conn an outbound returns;
  • the timeout is configurable as server.Config.TCPStallTimeout (default 10 s, negative disables it);
  • Close is idempotent, because two paths can now close the target.

The PR also adds an integration test. Four streams upload into targets that never read (one end of a net.Pipe()), then a new request to an echo server must complete on the same connection. Without the fix it times out after 10 s. With it, it passes in about 3.5 s, with the stall timeout set to 2 s for the test.

One gotcha while writing that test: with one stalled stream it passed even without the fix. One stream can only fill its own 8 MB window, not the 20 MB connection window. It takes three or four.

Results

In the loopback lab:

Server Target Streams New requests work again after
official v2.11.0 stall 6 never (> 30 s)
patched stall 6 7.8 s
patched stall 20 7.8 s
patched fast / slow / upclose — 0.0 s (no regression)

On the phone, we ran four speed tests in a row over 160 seconds on a patched server in Berlin. Hysteria2 was never declared dead. Before the patch it died at ~60 s every time, both in Berlin and on a server in Vilnius.

Rollout without an app update

Because the bug was on the server, the fix did not need a new app release. Our node image now builds Hysteria from the official source tag with the patch applied. We rolled it out the same night, one server at a time. Each server's VPN service restarted for about 2 seconds. Android, iOS, Windows and Linux users all got the fix at once.

Upstream

The bug is in the open-source Hysteria server, and its client-side half is in Xray, so every service that runs them is affected, not only ours. We reported both:

  • HyNetworks/hysteria#1702: the bug, how to reproduce it, and everything we ruled out.
  • HyNetworks/hysteria#1703: the fix on the current development branch, with the configurable timeout and the integration test.
  • XTLS/Xray-core#7169: the client side. A client that cancels the write side of a stream it no longer needs (CancelWrite, i.e. RESET_STREAM) would release the window even on servers without the fix. A contributor has since traced it on Xray's main branch, reproduced the stall on loopback, and plans a CancelWrite-based fix.

Limitations

  • The lab runs on loopback: no packet loss, no added latency. It shows the mechanism and the effect of the patch, not real-world timings.
  • The device result is one phone on one network, four speed tests over 160 seconds. Encouraging, not a long-term measurement.
  • For up to 10 seconds before the timer fires, TCP over that connection can still pause. The patch makes the stall short; it does not make it zero. A client-side fix would complement it.

Takeaways

  • "Connected but silent" usually means flow control. If ACKs and datagrams flow but stream data doesn't, look at windows before you blame the network.
  • A bigger window that only delays a failure is a clue, not a fix.
  • Make the destination's behaviour a test variable. Four target modes (fast, slow, upclose, stall) narrowed this down faster than any amount of packet reading.
  • Write the test that fails first. Ours passed until we used enough streams to exhaust the connection window, which taught us something about the bug itself.

If you run Hysteria2 and your users see TCP die after big uploads while DNS keeps working, this is probably it. The PR is small and easy to apply to v2.11.0.

Full report with setup details: lab.colitu.com/research/hysteria2-stall-after-upload. Our apps are open source at github.com/colitu. Questions and corrections are welcome in the comments.

title: Connecting React Hook Form to Spring Boot REST API: Clean DTO Validation & Global Exception Handling
description:
In modern full-stack development, client-side validation gives users instant feedback, but it must never be your only line of defense. Client checks can easily be bypassed using tools like cURL or Postman.

A secure, production-grade application requires robust server-side validation paired with clean, structured error feedback to the client.

In this tutorial, we will connect a React Hook Form frontend to a Spring Boot REST API using Jakarta Bean Validation (@Valid), centralize error handling with @RestControllerAdvice, and dynamically map backend field errors into React Hook Form using setError().

1. Architecture Overview 


text
[ React Hook Form ]                         [ Spring Boot Backend ]
        |                                              |
        | --- POST /api/users (Payload) -------------> | (Validates DTO via @Valid)
        |                                              |
        |                                         [ Validation Fails ]
        |                                              |
        |                                         MethodArgumentNotValidException
        |                                              |
        |                                         @RestControllerAdvice
        |                                              |
        | <--- 400 Bad Request { field: message } ---- |
        |                                              |
(Calls setError() to display messages)
2. Spring Boot 3 Backend Setup
Dependencies (pom.xml)
Ensure you have the Spring Boot Validation starter:

XML
<dependency>
    <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
    <artifactId>spring-boot-starter-validation</artifactId>
</dependency>
<dependency>
    <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
    <artifactId>spring-boot-starter-web</artifactId>
</dependency>
The Request DTO (UserRegistrationDto.java)
Define validation rules using standard Jakarta constraints:

Java
package com.example.demo.dto;

import jakarta.validation.constraints.Email;
import jakarta.validation.constraints.NotBlank;
import jakarta.validation.constraints.Size;

public class UserRegistrationDto {

    @NotBlank(message = "Username is required")
    @Size(min = 3, max = 20, message = "Username must be between 3 and 20 characters")
    private String username;

    @NotBlank(message = "Email address is required")
    @Email(message = "Please provide a valid email address")
    private String email;

    @NotBlank(message = "Password is required")
    @Size(min = 8, message = "Password must be at least 8 characters long")
    private String password;

    public String getUsername() { return username; }
    public void setUsername(String username) { this.username = username; }

    public String getEmail() { return email; }
    public void setEmail(String email) { this.email = email; }

    public String getPassword() { return password; }
    public void setPassword(String password) { this.password = password; }
}
Centralized Error Handler (GlobalExceptionHandler.java)
Intercept MethodArgumentNotValidException and transform the validation errors into a clean key-value map (fieldName: errorMessage):

Java
package com.example.demo.exception;

import org.springframework.http.HttpStatus;
import org.springframework.http.ResponseEntity;
import org.springframework.validation.FieldError;
import org.springframework.web.bind.MethodArgumentNotValidException;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.ExceptionHandler;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RestControllerAdvice;

import java.util.HashMap;
import java.util.Map;

@RestControllerAdvice
public class GlobalExceptionHandler {

    @ExceptionHandler(MethodArgumentNotValidException.class)
    public ResponseEntity<Map<String, String>> handleValidationExceptions(
            MethodArgumentNotValidException ex) {

        Map<String, String> errors = new HashMap<>();

        ex.getBindingResult().getAllErrors().forEach((error) -> {
            String fieldName = ((FieldError) error).getField();
            String errorMessage = error.getDefaultMessage();
            errors.put(fieldName, errorMessage);
        });

        return new ResponseEntity<>(errors, HttpStatus.BAD_REQUEST);
    }
}
The Controller (UserController.java)
Use @Valid to enforce validation before controller logic runs:

Java
package com.example.demo.controller;

import com.example.demo.dto.UserRegistrationDto;
import jakarta.validation.Valid;
import org.springframework.http.ResponseEntity;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.*;

import java.util.Map;

@RestController
@RequestMapping("/api/users")
@CrossOrigin(origins = "http://localhost:3000")
public class UserController {

    @PostMapping
    public ResponseEntity<?> registerUser(@Valid @RequestBody UserRegistrationDto userDto) {
        return ResponseEntity.ok(Map.of("message", "User registered successfully!"));
    }
}
3. React Frontend Integration
Install Axios and React Hook Form:

Bash
npm install axios react-hook-form
Registration Form Component (RegistrationForm.jsx)
When an HTTP 400 response is returned, iterate through the server error object and assign each error message to its corresponding field with setError:

JavaScript
import React from 'react';
import { useForm } from 'react-hook-form';
import axios from 'axios';

export default function RegistrationForm() {
  const {
    register,
    handleSubmit,
    setError,
    formState: { errors, isSubmitting },
    reset,
  } = useForm();

  const onSubmit = async (data) => {
    try {
      const response = await axios.post('http://localhost:8080/api/users', data);
      alert(response.data.message);
      reset();
    } catch (err) {
      if (err.response && err.response.status === 400) {
        const serverErrors = err.response.data;

        // Map backend errors dynamically into React Hook Form
        Object.keys(serverErrors).forEach((field) => {
          setError(field, {
            type: 'server',
            message: serverErrors[field],
          });
        });
      } else {
        alert('An unexpected error occurred. Please try again.');
      }
    }
  };

  return (
    <div style={{ maxWidth: '400px', margin: '40px auto', fontFamily: 'sans-serif' }}>
      <h2>Create an Account</h2>
      <form onSubmit={handleSubmit(onSubmit)} noValidate>

        {/* Username */}
        <div style={{ marginBottom: '16px' }}>
          <label style={{ display: 'block', marginBottom: '4px' }}>Username</label>
          <input
            type="text"
            {...register('username')}
            style={{ width: '100%', padding: '8px', boxSizing: 'border-box' }}
          />
          {errors.username && (
            <span style={{ color: 'red', fontSize: '12px' }}>{errors.username.message}</span>
          )}
        </div>

        {/* Email */}
        <div style={{ marginBottom: '16px' }}>
          <label style={{ display: 'block', marginBottom: '4px' }}>Email</label>
          <input
            type="email"
            {...register('email')}
            style={{ width: '100%', padding: '8px', boxSizing: 'border-box' }}
          />
          {errors.email && (
            <span style={{ color: 'red', fontSize: '12px' }}>{errors.email.message}</span>
          )}
        </div>

        {/* Password */}
        <div style={{ marginBottom: '16px' }}>
          <label style={{ display: 'block', marginBottom: '4px' }}>Password</label>
          <input
            type="password"
            {...register('password')}
            style={{ width: '100%', padding: '8px', boxSizing: 'border-box' }}
          />
          {errors.password && (
            <span style={{ color: 'red', fontSize: '12px' }}>{errors.password.message}</span>
          )}
        </div>

        <button
          type="submit"
          disabled={isSubmitting}
          style={{
            padding: '10px 16px',
            backgroundColor: '#0070f3',
            color: '#fff',
            border: 'none',
            borderRadius: '4px',
            cursor: 'pointer',
          }}
        >
          {isSubmitting ? 'Submitting...' : 'Register'}
        </button>
      </form>
    </div>
  );
}
Key Takeaways
DTO-Level Validation: Applying validation annotations directly to DTOs decouples business rules from database entity models.

Standardized Payloads: Returning a { fieldName: errorMessage } map keeps the API contract clean and straightforward to consume.

Seamless UI Integration: React Hook Form’s setError() updates the form state directly without manual re-render workarounds or custom state arrays.

Vercel is giving developers more options for running their backends on its platform. At its Ship conference in San Francisco
